text:
Jonas Siegenthaler is the Devils defenseman who never shows up in the box score and is quietly being robbed in it. He plays nearly 20 minutes a night on a team that has won eight of its last ten, he has 3 assists and no goals in 21 games, and he has taken nine shots all season. That's who he is: in 449 games before this season he scored 10 goals.

The number that matters is the gap between chances and results. With him on the ice, New Jersey has scored about 6.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve, one of our clearer "due" flags. At five on five the Devils take 55% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in his minutes. Goals have simply not followed. That kind of gap usually closes on its own.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why coaches trust him: he stopped 15% of the entries aimed at him last season against a typical 11%, and half his exits leave with possession. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year, so this is a steady role, not a hidden star.
